source_text: Domus Levitarum ius redemptionis perpetuum. Sacerdotium non alienatur. Amen.
thought_title: The Levites' house has a perpetual right of redemption
orientation: Origen is concluding his discussion of the redemption of houses in Leviticus, applying the rule about Levitical houses to the priesthood.
pass_a_gloss: House of [the] Levites [has] right of redemption perpetual. Priesthood not is alienated. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the legal force of ius as a right and the temporal force of perpetuum, matching the Levitical rule that Levite houses can always be redeemed.
Alienatur is a legal term for transfer of ownership; rendering it as 'is not alienated' preserves the sense that the priesthood cannot be permanently transferred away from the Levites.
rejected: The priesthood is not sold off

choices.why: Kept as a liturgical closing formula, as in the source.

bible_refs.note: The houses of the Levites have a perpetual right of redemption; the priesthood is not alienated.

pass_b_english: The house of the Levites has a perpetual right of redemption. The priesthood is not alienated. Amen.
